title: Helm and Kustomize

header.html: Use the Helm package manager to deploy existing packages; Kustomize
Kubernetes v1.37.0 (3-node test cluster, containerd 2.3.4); Helm v4.3.1; kubectl v1.36.1 with the built-in Kustomize v5.8.1

toc.title: Two ways to avoid copying YAML

html:
1Two ways to avoid copying YAML

Helm Kustomize
Idea a package (chart) with templates, filled in with values plain YAML base plus overlays that patch it
Result a release that Helm tracks (history, upgrade, rollback) ordinary objects, applied with kubectl apply -k
Typical use install software someone else packaged one app, several environments (dev, staging, prod)
On the exam docs allowed: helm.sh/docs docs allowed: kubernetes.io (kustomize pages)

2Helm in one page

A chart is a folder (or a .tgz) with Chart.yaml, values.yaml (the defaults) and templates/. A repository is a web server with an index.yaml listing charts. A release is one installation of a chart in a namespace, with a name.

Task Command
Add a repository helm repo add local http://127.0.0.1:8879
Refresh the index helm repo update
List repositories helm repo list
Search a repository helm search repo webapp (--versions for every version)
See the default values helm show values local/webapp
Install helm install shop local/webapp -n helm-ns --create-namespace --version 0.1.0
Override a value --set replicaCount=2 or --set service.type=NodePort
Values from a file -f prod-values.yaml (several -f allowed; later ones win)
Wait for readiness --wait --timeout 120s
List releases helm list -n helm-ns (-A for all namespaces)
Status of a release helm status shop -n helm-ns
Upgrade helm upgrade shop local/webapp -n helm-ns --set replicaCount=3
History and rollback helm history shop -n helm-ns, helm rollback shop 1 -n helm-ns
Values you supplied helm get values shop -n helm-ns (add --all for defaults too)
Rendered manifests of a release helm get manifest shop -n helm-ns
Render without installing helm template preview local/webapp --set replicaCount=4
Remove helm uninstall shop -n helm-ns

Always give -n <namespace> (releases live in a namespace; without it Helm uses the current one). The Deployment of a release is usually named <release>-<chart>, for example shop-webapp: read it from k get deploy -n helm-ns.

Precedence of values (low to high): the chart's values.yaml, then -f files (in order), then --set. helm upgrade keeps nothing from the earlier install unless you pass --reuse-values: repeat your --set flags or use --reuse-values.

Rollback creates a new revision. After install (1), upgrade (2) and rollback 1, helm history shows three revisions and the last one has the description "Rollback to 1".

Charts from a directory. helm install shop ./webapp installs a chart folder. helm create webapp makes a starter chart, helm lint ./webapp checks it, helm package ./webapp builds the .tgz, and helm pull local/webapp --untar downloads and unpacks one.

Exam tip

. Tasks name the release, the namespace, the chart and often a version or a value. Copy them exactly, then verify with helm list -n <ns> and k get deploy -n <ns>.

3Kustomize in one page

Kustomize reads a kustomization.yaml and builds the final YAML without templates.

kust/
├── base/
│   ├── deployment.yaml
│   ├── service.yaml
│   └── kustomization.yaml      # resources: [deployment.yaml, service.yaml]
└── overlays/
    └── prod/
        └── kustomization.yaml  # resources: [../../base] plus changes

# overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: prod            # set the namespace of every object
namePrefix: prod-          # prefix every name (nameSuffix also exists)
replicas:
- {name: web, count: 3}    # replica count of the Deployment `web`
images:
- {name: nginx, newTag: stable-alpine}
labels:
- pairs: {env: prod}       # add a label to all objects
  includeSelectors: false  # leave Service and Deployment selectors alone
Need Fields
Preview kubectl kustomize overlays/prod (builds, prints, changes nothing)
Apply kubectl apply -k overlays/prod
Delete kubectl delete -k overlays/prod
Add a ConfigMap configMapGenerator with literals or files; the name gets a hash suffix, and references in Pods are rewritten for you
Add a Secret secretGenerator
Change one field patches with target and a patch: JSON patch (op: add/replace/remove) or a strategic merge snippet
Change an image images (name, newName, newTag)
Shared annotations commonAnnotations 
configMapGenerator:
- name: web-config
  literals: [LEVEL=info]
patches:
- target: {kind: Deployment, name: web}
  patch: |-
    - op: add
      path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/envFrom
      value:
      - configMapRef: {name: web-config}

The generated ConfigMap is named web-config-<hash>; Kustomize changes the name in configMapRef to match, and a change to the data changes the hash, which restarts the Pods. Build with kubectl kustomize first to read errors; the usual ones are a wrong relative path in resources (../base versus ../../base), a typo in a field name, and a patch target that matches nothing.

Exam tip

. kubectl apply -k needs the directory that holds kustomization.yaml, not the file. Never edit the base when the task says to use an overlay.

4Helm or Kustomize?

  • "Install this chart / this version / with these values / roll it back": Helm.
  • "The same app in prod with 3 replicas and another image": Kustomize.
  • Both can be combined (Helm renders, Kustomize patches) but the exam keeps them separate.

5Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m06 -->

Lab 6.1: helm repo install

Domain: Deployment | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-01-helm-repo-install)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

A Helm chart repository is served at http://127.0.0.1:8879. Add it to Helm under the name local, refresh the index, and look at the available versions of the chart webapp. Install version 0.1.0 (not the newest) as the release shop in the namespace helm-ns (create the namespace with the install), with 2 replicas, by overriding the chart value replicaCount on the command line.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm repo add local http://127.0.0.1:8879
helm repo update
helm search repo local/webapp --versions
helm install shop local/webapp --version 0.1.0 -n helm-ns --create-namespace --set replicaCount=2 --wait --timeout 120s
helm list -n helm-ns

Lab 6.2: helm upgrade rollback

Domain: Deployment | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-02-helm-upgrade-rollback)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The release app (chart local/webapp version 0.1.0, 1 replica) is installed in the namespace helm-ns; the repository local is already added. Upgrade the release to chart version 0.2.0 with 3 replicas. Then the upgrade turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run chart 0.1.0 with 1 replica, and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm upgrade app local/webapp --version 0.2.0 -n helm-ns --set replicaCount=3 --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns
helm rollback app 1 -n helm-ns --wait --timeout 120s
helm history app -n helm-ns

Lab 6.3: helm values file

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-03-helm-values-file)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The file ~/work/prod-values.yaml holds the settings for production. Install the newest version of the chart local/webapp (the repository local is already added) as the release site in the namespace helm-ns (create it with the install), taking the values from that file. Do not edit the file.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm show values local/webapp | head -20
helm install site local/webapp -n helm-ns --create-namespace -f ~/work/prod-values.yaml --wait --timeout 120s
helm get values site -n helm-ns

Lab 6.4: helm uninstall values

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-04-helm-uninstall-values)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Two releases exist in the namespace helm-ns: old and keep. Remove the release old completely. Save the user-supplied values of the release keep (not the chart defaults) to the file ~/answers/keep-values.yaml.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm list -n helm-ns
helm uninstall old -n helm-ns
helm get values keep -n helm-ns > ~/answers/keep-values.yaml
cat ~/answers/keep-values.yaml

Lab 6.5: helm show values template

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-05-helm-show-values-template)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Without installing anything: (1) find the default value of image.repository in the chart local/webapp (the repository local is already added) and write only that value to ~/answers/repo.txt; (2) render the manifests of the chart for a release named preview with 4 replicas and save the output to ~/answers/rendered.yaml.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

helm show values local/webapp | grep -A3 "^image:"
echo nginx > ~/answers/repo.txt
helm template preview local/webapp --set replicaCount=4 > ~/answers/rendered.yaml
grep -E "replicas|name: preview" ~/answers/rendered.yaml

Lab 6.6: kustomize overlay

Domain: Deployment | Points: 7 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-06-kustomize-overlay)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

A Kustomize base exists in ~/kust/base (a Deployment web with 1 replica and a Service web). Create an overlay in ~/kust/overlays/prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, 3 replicas, and the container image to nginx:stable-alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

cat > ~/kust/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml <<'Y'
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: prod
namePrefix: prod-
replicas:
- {name: web, count: 3}
images:
- {name: nginx, newTag: stable-alpine}
Y
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/prod | head -30
kubectl create ns prod
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/prod
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment prod-web --timeout=120s

Lab 6.7: kustomize config generator

Domain: Deployment | Points: 8 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-07-kustomize-config-generator)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

A Kustomize base exists in ~/kust/base (a Deployment web and a Service web). Create an overlay in ~/kust/overlays/staging that reuses the base and: sets the namespace staging, generates a ConfigMap named web-config with the literal LEVEL=info, and patches the Deployment so that its container loads all keys of that ConfigMap as environment variables (envFrom). Do not edit the base. Create the namespace staging and apply the overlay. The running Pod must show LEVEL=info in its environment.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

cat > ~/kust/overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml <<'Y'
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: staging
configMapGenerator:
- name: web-config
  literals:
  - LEVEL=info
patches:
- target: {kind: Deployment, name: web}
  patch: |-
    - op: add
      path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/envFrom
      value:
      - configMapRef:
          name: web-config
Y
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/staging | head -40
kubectl create ns staging
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/staging
kubectl -n staging rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n staging exec deploy/web -- printenv LEVEL

Lab 6.8: fix kustomize overlay

Domain: Deployment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m06-08-fix-kustomize-overlay)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The overlay ~/kust/overlays/prod fails with kubectl apply -k. Fix the overlay (do not change the base) so that it deploys the Deployment prod-web (name prefix prod-) and the Service prod-web into the namespace prod, with 2 replicas. Create the namespace prod and apply the overlay.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/prod 2>&1 | head -3
sed -i 's#^- ../base#- ../../base#' ~/kust/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/prod | head -12
kubectl create ns prod
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/prod
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment prod-web --timeout=120s

<!-- /LABS -->

6Recall questions

R1What is a Helm release?

Show the answer

One installation of a chart in a namespace, with a name and a history of revisions.

R2Which command shows the default values of a chart?

Show the answer

helm show values <repo>/<chart>.

R3How do you install a specific chart version?

Show the answer

helm install <release> <repo>/<chart> --version <x.y.z>.

R4Which value source wins: a -f file or --set?

Show the answer

--set wins over -f files, which win over the chart defaults.

R5How do you see only the values you supplied to a release?

Show the answer

helm get values <release> (add --all for the chart defaults too).

R6How do you render a chart without installing it?

Show the answer

helm template <release> <chart> [--set ...].

R7Which command applies a Kustomize overlay, and which one only prints it?

Show the answer

kubectl apply -k <dir> applies; kubectl kustomize <dir> prints.

R8What does namePrefix do, and why does a generated ConfigMap name have a hash?

Show the answer

It prefixes every object name; the hash changes when the data changes, so Pods that use the ConfigMap restart.
